title: Greater Manchester Mayor eyes 2050 underground trains opening date

input.lead: Bev Craig says the city region needs to plan for the future and this means going underground
input.summary: Bev Craig says the city region needs to plan for the future and this means going underground
input.evidence_text: Plans to create Greater Manchester's own London Underground-style transport system have been backed by mayor Bev Craig, with 2050 eyed as a potential opening date The scheme could cost tens of billions and take decades to build - with the need for government backing - but has been described by Craig as the "only option" for the county's future Transport for Greater Manchester's (TfGM) timeline for the project could see detailed plans and a business case ready by 2030, with a push to start building by around 2040 and a 2050 opening date Craig said: "In Greater Manchester we've started planning for what future is possible, and that means going underground." The idea was separate from demands from city leaders in Manchester for an underground railway station at Manchester Piccadilly, which would play a part in boosting railway travel supporting the £45bn Northern Powerhouse Rail project But a new underground station at Piccadilly is seen as an essential "first step" ahead of wider plans for Greater Manchester, including the potential for a future underground tube network

input.summary: Homelessness Rough sleeping rises in Greater Manchester as Andy Burnham pledges to end crisis by Christmas The number of rough sleepers across Greater Manchester went up in June, new figures show, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to get every rough Comments News Paul Gallagher
input.evidence_text: Homelessness Rough sleeping rises in Greater Manchester as Andy Burnham pledges to end crisis by Christmas The number of rough sleepers across Greater Manchester went up in June, new figures show, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to get every rough Comments News Paul Gallagher 05:57, 14 Sep 2026 The number of people sleeping rough across Greater Manchester has reached one of its highest levels in six years, according to new data released as former mayor Andy Burnham pledged to make homelessness a national priority Government data shows there were 444 rough sleepers across the ten boroughs of Greater Manchester in June 2026, up from 402 in June 2025 - a rise of 42 people, or 10.4 per cent. It is the highest figure for June, and the fourth highest monthly total since October 2020 The figures land as Mr Burnham - who made ending rough sleeping his first pledge on entering Downing Street in July - is pushing ahead with a national drive to get every rough sleeper off the streets by Christmas , backed by a £442 million funding package The biggest driver of the rise in Greater Manchester was Manchester city itself, where the number of rough sleepers in June jumped from 149 last summer to 195 - an increase of 46 people Tameside saw the second sharpest rise, climbing from 21 to 33, while Trafford rose from 6 to 10 and Bury edged up from 29 to 31. Not all boroughs saw increases. Salford , Oldham , Rochdale and Bolton recorded slightly lower numbers sleeping rough on their streets

The incredible fights; the cheeky sense of humour; the big heart trying to come to terms with a tortured soul We loved him - whether we were United fans or followers of his beloved Manchester City - because of his sporting prowess; his unashamed Manc personality; and his brave and very public fight against his personal demons No, it is perhaps fitting for this famously humble son of Hyde that he will be remembered privately, at people's homes or in the pubs where there will be a laugh and a joke and a tear in the eye as a glass is raised in remembrance It will be an especially difficult day for Ricky's family and, of course, for his parents Carol and Ray, who will try their best to remember the funny episodes and the good times they shared with 'Richard'. They have admitted they're still tortured by 'what if' thoughts

It is the highest figure for June, and the fourth highest monthly total since October 2020 The figures land as Mr Burnham - who made ending rough sleeping his first pledge on entering Downing Street in July - is pushing ahead with a national drive to get every rough sleeper off the streets by Christmas , backed by a £442 million funding package The biggest driver of the rise in Greater Manchester was Manchester city itself, where the number of rough sleepers in June jumped from 149 last summer to 195 - an increase of 46 people Tameside saw the second sharpest rise, climbing from 21 to 33, while Trafford rose from 6 to 10 and Bury edged up from 29 to 31. input.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

input.evidence_text: Works will soon begin to ensure the preservation and protection of one of Manchester city centre’s most recognised landmarks For nearly four decades, the iconic Chinatown archway has stood as the gateway to the city’s famous Chinatown. In recent years, some elements have degraded, posing a risk to the arch itself and to the safety of the public who pass beneath To carry out repairs, materials and artisans from China will be sourced so that every facet of its restoration remains true to the culture which it honours. This is part of a wider regeneration of the Chinatown area as the Council works to invest more into the amenity and upkeep Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin, Executive Member for Clean Air, Environment and Transport, said: “For generations this arch has been a focal point for the Chinese community in Manchester. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
